# A timer under a loop reads the element its copy holds now, after the list
# changed: `rows` drops its first element, so the copy at 0 holds 2, and no
# tick after the click may push 1.
#
# android rendered each timer where it was written as a LaunchedEffect, which
# outlives the composition that started it, so its handler kept the loop
# variable of its first composition and went on pushing 1. It runs the latest
# composition's handler (rememberUpdatedState) now.
#
# bubbletea's test invokers ran the key's Update and dropped the commands it
# returned, so the click -- its Update armed each copy's tick -- left every
# schedule marked live with nothing to tick it, and none ever ticked. An
# invoker runs them as a waiting test runs the Model's; and a message for a
# Model another test held is dropped rather than delivered to it.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main ui.node {
    var rows = [1, 2, 3]
    var seen list[int] = []
    for var r = rows {
        time.timer(interval=20ms, @tick {
            seen.push(r)
        })
        ui.text(value="{r}")
    }
    ui.button #drop(text="drop", @click {
        rows = [2, 3]
        seen = []
    })
}

func testATimerReadsItsCopysVariableAfterTheListChanges(t Test, c main) {
    c.drop.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.seen.length() >= 6, 3000)
    t.assert(c.seen.length() >= 6)
    t.assert(!c.seen.contains(1))
}

ui.window {
    main
}
